# Manchester United Land Ugarte in €50m Deal from PSG

Manchester United completed the signing of Manuel Ugarte for €50m (£42m) plus €10m in bonuses from Paris Saint-Germain on Friday evening, with the Uruguayan promising to "fight for trophies" and help return the club to elite level.

The 23-year-old signed a five-year contract with the option of a further 12 months. He is Erik ten Hag's fifth major acquisition of the window and gives the manager a second senior No 6, alongside Casemiro.

Ugarte said: "It is an incredible feeling to join a club of this magnitude – one that is admired all around the world. The project that the football leadership discussed with me is extremely exciting. Manchester United is an ambitious club and I am an ambitious player.

"I know how incredible United fans are and I cannot wait to experience Old Trafford. I'm someone who is so determined to succeed. I will sacrifice and give everything for my teammates. Together we will fight to win trophies and reach the level where this club needs to be."

Dan Ashworth, United's sporting director, said: "Signing Manuel was another of our primary targets for this summer. His arrival reflects the strategic recruitment approach we have implemented since the new structure was put in place. Manuel brings exceptional defensive qualities, tactical intelligence, and a relentless work ethic that perfectly complements the squad Erik is building. At just 23, he represents both immediate quality and long-term value for the club."

Ugarte's arrival had been weeks in the making, with negotiations between United and PSG stretching through much of August. The Uruguay international, who joined the French champions only last summer from Sporting CP for around €60m, had fallen down the pecking order under Luis Enrique, who preferred a different midfield profile in his system. That opened the door for United to swoop, with Ten Hag long viewing a defensive midfielder as a critical piece of his rebuild.

Known for his tenacious tackling, ball recovery numbers and aggressive pressing, Ugarte led Europe's top five leagues in tackles per game during his final season at Sporting. Those attributes are precisely what United have lacked in central midfield, where Casemiro endured a difficult campaign and Sofyan Amrabat's loan spell underwhelmed.

Ugarte is expected to be available for selection after the international break, with Ten Hag likely to integrate him gradually. He joins Leny Yoro, Joshua Zirkzee, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui among United's summer arrivals as the club continue their ambitious overhaul under the new INEOS-led ownership structure.

For Ten Hag, who survived a difficult end-of-season review to retain his position, Ugarte's signing represents a significant vote of confidence and a clear signal that the squad is being shaped in his image. The pressure now turns to results on the pitch, where United must demonstrate that this summer's heavy investment can translate into a genuine return to the Premier League's upper reaches.
